Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuregex 0.1.0

  • Initial CRAN submission.

The engine

  • Bundles PCRE2 10.48, the 8-bit library with its JIT compiler, built without CMake and with every PCRE2 symbol hidden from R’s own copy. zuregex_info() reports the version, whether the JIT compiler works on this machine, OpenMP, the thread cap and the cache size.

Compiling

  • re_compile() compiles patterns with flag letters, a JavaScript dialect, literal patterns and JIT compilation into re objects, which survive saveRDS(). re_info() describes them, and re_escape() quotes metacharacters.
  • \C, which matches one byte, is a compile error in a pattern matched as UTF-8, because it could split a character. Bytes patterns allow it.
  • Patterns are cached, 128 by default; re_cache_size() and re_cache_clear() manage the cache.

Matching

  • re_detect(), re_count(), re_locate() and re_locate_all() match character vectors, raw vectors and lists of raw vectors, with one pattern for every element or one per element. Offsets are one-based and inclusive, in characters or bytes.
  • re_extract(), re_extract_all(), re_match() and re_match_all() return matches and capture groups as vectors and data frames built in C. re_match() types its columns through proto, as utils::strcapture() does.
  • Every verb takes flags and literal, as re_compile() does, so re_detect(x, "abc", flags = "i") is base R’s ignore.case = TRUE and literal = TRUE is its fixed = TRUE. An re object carries its own.
  • re_replace() uses PCRE2’s extended templates ($1, ${name}, ${1:-default}, ${1:+yes:no}, case forcing), literal text, or a function called once with every match. re_expand() expands a template with the first match, and re_split() splits as Python’s re.split() does.
  • re_limits() bounds the work of a match, per call or through the zuregex.limits option. An element that hits a limit raises zuregex_error_limit, or gives NA and one warning with on_limit = "na".
  • Matching runs on several threads with OpenMP on large inputs, with the same results on any number of threads; re_threads() caps them. On macOS that uses the libomp R ships, as CRAN builds it. zuregex_info() reports whether OpenMP is on, the threads and cores it can use, and the input size below which a call stays on one thread. A forked child, such as a parallel::mclapply() worker, matches on one thread.
  • Each call does little work outside the match itself. Subjects that R marks as ASCII skip PCRE2’s UTF-8 check, results are built in one buffer per thread, and a call with one pattern string is a single .Call. Extraction and captures are 10 to 40 times faster than base R’s perl = TRUE. Detection, replacement, splitting and calls on a few strings run about level with base R and stringi, a little ahead or behind depending on the platform.
  • Errors are classed conditions inheriting from zuregex_error.

For other packages

  • A C API through LinkingTo: zuregex and <zuregex-r.h>: compile, match, read offsets, substitute and set limits through opaque zr_pattern and zr_match_data handles, so an upgrade of the bundled PCRE2 never changes a consumer’s build. Offsets there are zero-based, half-open and in bytes.
